title: SRE status sentinel — communications runbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, flexible draft for incident communications that covers: quick public status posts, customer-targeted outreach, and an internal war-room checklist for first 60/180 minutes. Meant for oncall to adapt and send; keep the tone consistent, factual, and customer-centric.

Signal tiers (quick):
- P0 (showstopper): total outage or data loss, broad customer impact
- P1 (major degradation): core features degraded for many customers, partial impact
- P2 (localized): single-region or small subset impacted, workaround exists
- P3 (informational): nonblocking degradation or scheduled maintenance

Status page templates (minimal, 3 updates):
1) Initial (within 10 min):
- Title: Investigating: service disruption affecting inference endpoints
- Body: We are aware of increased errors and higher latency for some API requests. Our SRE and backend teams are investigating. No action required from customers right now. Impact: potential failed API responses and elevated latency for requests to hosted-api in us-west-2. Affected customers: subset of production traffic. Next update: 30 minutes.
- Metadata: components: api/redwood-hosted, affected_regions: us-west-2, incident_id: INFR-<auto-id>

2) Update (every 30–60 min):
- Title: Update: root cause identified, mitigation in progress
- Body: We identified a bad scaling decision on autoscaler causing overloaded inference pools. Mitigation: draining and restarting affected nodes and shifting traffic to reserved capacity while hotfix deploy rolls out. Expected restoration: 45–90 minutes. Temporary workaround: use dedicated region routing or retry with exponential backoff.
- Action for customers: none required unless you see sustained errors — open support ticket.

3) Resolved:
- Title: Resolved: API latency and error rates returned to normal
- Body: The mitigation completed (nodes drained and control-plane fix deployed). Monitoring indicates normal error rates and latency. Root cause summary and follow-up postmortem (link) will be published within 72 hours. If you continue to see issues, contact support.

Customer-facing email/snippet (P0/P1 high impact):
- Subject: Incident update: temporary API disruption (resolved/in progress)
- Greeting: Hi — we want to be transparent about a recent issue that affected Redwood Inference.
- Short summary: Between 2025-02-25 14:05 and 15:10 UTC, a subset of API requests experienced higher error rates and latency due to autoscaler misconfiguration.
- What we did: our oncall team implemented traffic shifts and a hotfix; most customers saw restored service by 15:10 UTC.
- Customer impact: brief description (affected endpoints, retry guidance, data integrity note).
- Next steps: full postmortem in 72 hours with mitigation plan and timeline for permanent fix.
- Contact: support@redwood.ai with incident id INFR-<id>.

Internal war-room checklist (first 60 minutes):
- T+0: Triage lead acknowledges and assigns roles (comm lead, triage, mitigation, logs). Create channel: #incident-INFR-<id>.
- 0–10m: Post initial status page and Slack announcement (template above). Ensure customer-success knows (tag #cs-ops).
- 10–30m: Triage: gather logs (elk/stack query keys), identify error signatures, confirm blast radius (regions/customers). Owner: logs lead.
- 20–40m: Mitigation plan: if heavy CPU/GPU saturation, trigger autoscaler rollback or route to dedicated pools. Owner: infra-sre.
- 30–60m: Implement mitigation, validate with synthetic checks, update status page. If customer SLA at risk, open a customer bridge and notify account owners.
- Always: include timestamps for actions, list commands executed, and capture terminal logs as notes.

Quick checklist of useful commands/links (fill with org-specific commands):
- Check queue/backlog: /infra metrics tail --component inference-pool
- Force route to dedicated: /routing set --pool dedicated --selector region:us-west-2
- Restart rolling nodes: /infra nodes drain --label affected=true && /infra nodes restart --selector affected=true
- Synthetic test: curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health/check

Tone & escalation rules (comm lead):
- Be concise, avoid speculation, surface concrete impact, expected timelines, and clear next update ETA.
- If legal/personal-data exposure suspected, pause public post and escalate to security/compliance.

Post-incident follow-up (postmortem stub):
- Owner: incident lead
- Sections to include: timeline, scope/impact, root cause, mitigation steps, monitoring gaps, customer impact summary, action items (owner + due date), verification plan. Publish to Confluence and link from status page.

Open questions / TODOs for doc:
- Decide canonical shortlink format for status pages vs. Confluence postmortem.
- Confirm exact autoscaler rollback command with infra team.
- Add localized customer templates for enterprise customers with dedicated contacts.

References & hooks:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Incident+Framework
- Current canonical escalation: JIRA INFR-421
- Oncall rotation: https://hr.redwood.ai/oncall

Notes to self (working):
- Keep templates short — customers appreciate clarity.
- Practice runbook at next SRE DR drill.
- Add a small field in status posts for "estimated affected customers" to improve CS routing.

End of draft.
